Create exactly TWO new files:
  1. deploy/fedbench-backup.service
  2. deploy/fedbench-backup.timer

systemd units that run deploy/backup-fedbench.sh nightly. READ that script first -- its arguments
and exit codes are the contract. Read deploy/tailscale-cert.service and .timer for the house shape
of a oneshot-plus-timer pair, and follow it.

Requirements, each with its reason as a comment in the unit:
* Type=oneshot. A backup is a task that finishes, not a daemon.
* NO Restart= and NO [Install] section on the .service. Restarting a finished oneshot restarts a
  completed task, and a timer-driven service with its own [Install] would run a backup on every
  boot. The TIMER carries WantedBy=timers.target; it is the thing that gets enabled.
  tests/deployUnitSafety.test.ts enforces exactly this pairing and will fail the build otherwise.
* Runs as a non-root user that can read the database and write the backup directory. Say which and
  why in a comment; do NOT invent a new account -- use one that exists per the FACTS block.
* Persistent=true on the timer, so a backup missed while the box was down runs at next boot rather
  than being skipped silently. An overnight outage must not cost a night's backup without saying so.
* A randomized delay, so the backup does not start at the same instant as every other timer.
* Sensible hardening that does not break it: ProtectSystem, PrivateTmp, NoNewPrivileges, and
  ReadWritePaths for the backup directory ONLY. Note in a comment that ProtectHome must not be
  strict enough to block reading what it needs.
* OnCalendar at a time that does not collide with the existing tailscale-cert.timer (04:40).

Do not write an install script and do not modify any other file.

LIVE STATE ON edaserver, 2026-09-11, verified from a separate tailnet device:
  * https://edaserver.tailcb2a72.ts.net — Caddy on 443, bound ONLY to the tailnet addresses
    (100.87.250.124 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::2032:fa7d), asserted against the kernel after start.
  * /rest/v1/* and /storage/v1/* -> nginx shim on 127.0.0.1:8087 -> PostgREST 3000 / fed_storage 3001
  * /api/* and /healthz -> vault-api on 127.0.0.1:8099, running as the vaultsvc system account
  * /healthz returns {"ok":true,"checks":{"database":{"ok":true,"field_definitions":32}}}
  * Unauthenticated data-plane requests are refused with Postgres 42501 as HTTP 401, never [].
  * /api/* returns 401 even for routes that do not exist: authentication runs before routing.
  * Database fedbench, 19 migrations. connect.health is all zeros because no vault DATA has been
    migrated from hosted Supabase yet; connect.kinds is seeded (7 rows) and is the liveness probe.

SERVICE ACCOUNTS AND PATHS:
  * fedbackup owns /srv/fedbackup (which IS its home, so everything under it is SELinux
    user_home_t) and runs fed-postgrest and fed-storage.
  * vaultsvc is a system account with NO home directory, deliberately. It owns /srv/vault/app.
  * The live object root is /srv/fedbench/objects. /srv/nextcloud/fedbench/objects is the nightly
    COLD ARCHIVE on a single non-redundant 7.3T disk and must never be served live.
  * psql is at /usr/pgsql-17/bin/psql. A bare `psql` resolves to the one Siemens Calibre ships.

SHELL RULES, learned the hard way on this box:
  * LF only. A CR breaks bash at the first `for ... ; do` as `syntax error near unexpected token
    $'do\r'`, and systemd does not strip a trailing CR from a unit either.
  * NEVER write a literal backslash-n where a line continuation belongs: bash reads it as an
    escaped `n` and silently appends an argument. tests/deployScripts.test.ts fails the build on
    both of those and on any stray control byte.
  * `set -uo pipefail`, never `set -e`: a failed check must be REPORTED, not abort the run half way.
  * A pipeline's exit status belongs to the LAST command. `cmd | tail` hides cmd's failure -- that
    made a failed `npm ci` report as success here today.

Create exactly ONE new file:
  1. tests/backupScript.test.ts

A vitest suite over deploy/backup-fedbench.sh. Read that script first and read two existing tests
in tests/ (deployScripts, applyMigrations) to match style.

Pin these, each because getting it wrong loses data quietly:

1. IT NEVER PRUNES AFTER A FAILED DUMP. Retention deletes old backups; doing that when tonight's
   dump failed turns one bad night into the loss of every good one. Assert the prune is guarded by
   the dump's success.
2. IT WRITES BOTH FORMATS -- a pg_dump custom-format archive AND a plain .sql.gz twin. A -Fc dump
   needs a matching-or-newer pg_restore forever; a .sql.gz is readable by zgrep, by a human, and by
   any future Postgres. Losing the ability to read your own backup is a way to lose data.
3. IT VERIFIES THE DUMP before counting the run a success -- non-empty, and readable by
   `pg_restore --list`. A zero-byte or truncated dump nobody opened is the classic backup failure.
4. IT SAYS IT IS NOT A SECOND PHYSICAL COPY, on every run and not only in a comment. Dumps on the
   database's own host do not clear the cutover gate, and a backup that quietly looks sufficient is
   worse than none because it retires the question in somebody's head. Assert the script PRINTS
   that, i.e. the text appears in an echo/printf and not merely in a `#` comment.
5. It uses the absolute psql/pg_dump paths, not bare names.

Assert the script exists and exceeds a minimum length in its own `it` -- every check above is a
text search, and a text search over a missing file passes while verifying nothing.

For check 4, strip comment lines before searching, and add an `it` proving the stripper works, so a
sentence that appears ONLY in a comment cannot satisfy it. That distinction is the entire point of
the check.

Run `npx vitest run tests/backupScript.test.ts` until it reflects the truth about the file.

Create exactly ONE new file:
  1. tests/migrateVaultData.test.ts

A vitest suite over scripts/migrate-vault-data.mjs, which copies the hosted Supabase vault into the
self-hosted one. Read it first, and match the style of existing tests in tests/.

This script will be run ONCE, against irreplaceable data, by someone who cannot easily undo it. The
properties below are the reason it is safe to run at all:

1. IT NEVER WRITES TO THE SOURCE. Assert no DELETE or PATCH request is issued against the SOURCE_*
   URLs anywhere in the file. The hosted projects remain the system of record until something else
   has demonstrably replaced them; a migration that can mutate its source is one bad flag away from
   destroying the only copy.
2. KEYSET PAGING, NOT OFFSET. Assert it uses an `id=gt.` style cursor and does NOT use `offset` or
   `.range(` for pagination. Offset paging against a table receiving inserts silently SKIPS rows,
   and a migration that silently skips rows is worse than one that fails.
3. BLOBS BEFORE ROWS. Assert the ordering is objects-then-rows. Blobs-first can only leave an
   object with no row, which is classifiable and fixed by re-running; rows-first leaves a row
   pointing at an object that does not exist, which every consumer treats as corruption.
4. IT VERIFIES BY HASH, NOT SIZE. Assert sha256 appears and that a size comparison is not the
   integrity check. A truncated-then-resumed transfer that lands on the same length is invisible to
   a size check.
5. `--dry-run` exists and is documented as the first step.

Assert the file exists and exceeds a minimum length in its own `it`.

Include an `it` for each detector showing it fires against a small inline string containing the bad
form -- an offset paging call, a DELETE to a source URL. A check that cannot fail is not a check.

If the script genuinely violates one of these, that is a REAL finding and exactly what this test is
for: leave the assertion failing, and say so clearly. Do not edit the script.

Run `npx vitest run tests/migrateVaultData.test.ts`.

Modify exactly ONE file:
  1. scripts/smoke.sh

This is the end-to-end walk: schema, sample, measurement, upload, register, include=files,
download, delete, verify 404. It takes VAULT_API_URL and VAULT_API_KEY from the environment. The
endpoint is now LIVE, so this script can finally be run for real -- update it so that running it is
straightforward and its failures are legible.

Add, without changing the flow it already tests:
* A header comment giving the real invocation against the live endpoint:
      VAULT_API_URL=https://edaserver.tailcb2a72.ts.net VAULT_API_KEY=<key> bash scripts/smoke.sh
  and noting the key lives in /etc/vault/vault-api.env on the server, readable only by root.

  would otherwise fail in a more confusing way than "the database check is failing", and the reader
  would start debugging the wrong thing.

  up after itself, and make any failure to clean up loud rather than silent -- a smoke test that
  leaves debris in the system of record is a smoke test people stop running.
* Preserve `set -uo pipefail` semantics if present; do not introduce `set -e`.
